analysis_reasoning: MCTS Round 2 expands node opt-round-1 (mean reward 1.7403, visit 1). Parent hit 5.6991x geomean with a fused chunk-recurrence kernel but used a hand-tuned BV heuristic: BV=64 when chunk_size<=64 else BV=32. Hypothesis: on cs=128 shapes this leaves headroom. Offline empirical BV sweep over ALL 8 shapes (dense + varlen, cs 64/128) on the actual parent kernel disproves the parent heuristic: BV=64 is the fastest config on EVERY shape, including the four cs=128 cases where parent ran BV=32. Measured (ms/kernel): case2 cs128 0.280(BV64) vs 0.463(BV32) = 1.65x; case4 cs128 3.19 vs 5.12 = 1.61x; case6 cs128 0.913 vs 1.33 = 1.46x; case8 varlen cs128 7.86 vs 13.5 = 1.72x. BV=128 is never better than BV=64. The cs=128 shapes are exactly the weakest per-shape speedups (2.9-3.5x). Fix = set BV=min(64,V) uniformly, preserving min() guard and V%BV==0 (all shapes V=128). num_warps autotune is infeasible on Ascend (validated: fixed at 4); manual-config triton.autotune over BV would select BV=64 for every shape but adds ~7s/shape autotune overhead and D7 forbids toggling multibuffer off, so a hand-tuned BV=64 reproduces the autotune optimum with zero runtime cost.
